model_interpretation.claim: Dynamic scheduling of one complete row at a time may reduce imbalance from rows with different Mandelbrot iteration counts compared with contiguous static row allocation. The serial branch avoids OpenMP overhead when the usable team is one; capping the team by height avoids requesting workers that cannot receive rows. The recurrence and per-pixel coordinate expressions remain unchanged.

items.subject: Thread-budgeted OpenMP work decomposition
items.objective: Explore OpenMP work decomposition without changing the scalar pixel recurrence. Contrast static contiguous rows with dynamic/guided row scheduling and, if useful, a contiguous 2D tiled or collapsed-loop partition to test whether row granularity leaves imbalance within expensive rows. Vary chunk sizes only as measured experiments. Use a serial path when it avoids one-thread overhead; never exceed `threads` or change global OpenMP settings. Preserve the original float coordinate and recurrence behavior, write every output, and do not specialize to tested bounds or dimensions. Validate smaller and shifted-bound cases; measure native wall time at one and four cores, including scheduling overhead at n=1024.
